chunks: From him, from Salih, from Muhammad ibn Awramah, from Ibn Sinan, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said:

I, along with my partner Al-Qasim, and Najm ibn Hateem, and Salih ibn Sahl, were in Medina. We were debating regarding the Lordship (Rububiyya). Some of us said to the others, 'What are we doing with this? We are close to him, and none of us is in dissimulation (taqiyyah). Let us go to him.' He said, so we stood up. By Allah, we had not reached the door when he had come out to us without shoes or a gown, every hair on his head was standing up, and he was saying: 'No, no! O Mufazzal, and O Al-Qasim, and O Najm. No, no! But they are honored servants who do not precede Him in speech, and they act according to His command.'

key_terms.لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ: Do not precede Him in speech

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say to his companions when they were debating the concept of Lordship?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia doctrine of *Rububiyya* (Lordship) through the Imam's spontaneous correction of companions who were debating his status while in close proximity. The Imam’s disheveled appearance and urgent declaration that he is merely an 'honored servant' (*Abdun Mukarram*) who does not precede God in speech (*La Yasbiquna*) underscores the principle of *Tawhid* in action, distinguishing the Imam's unique authority from absolute divine sovereignty. This narrative serves as a practical demonstration of how the Imam embodies the Quranic ideal of perfect servitude while holding the position of God's vicegerent.
